user_goal.request: Explain how water movement across the cell membrane changes the firmness of a plant cell.

observation.reason: C1-C4 are generic textbook osmosis/turgor/plasmolysis/RWC statements, but the only cited source (E_6fb69a1cc780, a Kentucky bluegrass ethephon drought-tolerance transcriptome study) is about drought tolerance and ethephon treatment; its abstract does not state the osmosis definition, turgor pressure pushing the protoplast against the cell wall, plasmolysis/membrane detachment, or RWC as an indicator of cell firmness. Entailment is therefore not established for any claim, and the required entities (cell membrane, cell wall, central vacuole, cytoplasm/protoplast, water potential, turgor pressure) and required dynamic mechanisms (osmotic water movement, turgor build-up, plasmolysis/wilting) are not covered by verified evidence. Since the core mechanistic explanation and learning objectives lack source support, no fact can be passed while blocking issues remain.
